chunks: Ali ibn Hatim from Ali ibn Sulayman al-Zurari said: He narrated to us Ahmad ibn Ishaq from Sadan ibn Muslim from Abu Basir who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:
Pray eight rak'ahs on the twentieth of the month of Ramadan after Maghrib, and twelve rak'ahs after 'Atamah (late night prayer).
When it is the night in which what is hoped for is hoped for (Laylat al-Qadr), pray one hundred rak'ahs, reciting 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad' ten times in each rak'ah.
I said: May I be your ransom, if I cannot stand, he said: Then sit. I said: If I cannot sit, he said: Then pray while lying on your bed.

key_terms.بعد العتمة: After the late night prayer (Isha or a specific late prayer)
key_terms.قل هو الله أحد: The chapter 'He is Allah, One' (Surah Al-Ikhlas)
key_terms.ليلة التي يرجى فيها ما يرجى: The night in which what is hoped for is hoped for (referring to Laylat al-Qadr)
key_terms.مستلقٍ على فراشك: Lying on your back on your bed

ai.seo_question: What are the specific night prayers and their rulings for the last ten nights of Ramadan according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* details the specific night prayers for the 20th, 21st, and 23rd nights of Ramadan, with the 23rd night (Laylat al-Qadr) featuring a unique 100-rak'ah prayer where Surah Al-Ikhlas is recited ten times per unit. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the distinct spiritual status of these 'Nights of Hope' and provides practical jurisprudential concessions (rukhan) for physical weakness, allowing prayer while seated or lying down. The repetition of Al-Ikhlas underscores the centrality of divine unity in the devotion of the final third of Ramadan.
